name: Flood / basin irrigation
description: Water flows over the field or into basins around plants.
notes: Simple but uses the most water; level fields well.

name: Furrow irrigation
description: Water flows in furrows between ridges.
notes: Suits row crops like cotton, maize, sugarcane; skip-furrow saves water.

name: Drip irrigation
description: Water is delivered near roots through emitters.
notes: Saves water, allows fertigation; clean filters and flush laterals regularly.

name: Sprinkler irrigation
description: Water is sprayed like rain.
notes: Suits pulses, groundnut and uneven land; avoid in high wind.

name: Rain gun
description: Large sprinkler covering a wide radius.
notes: Suits sugarcane and fodder; needs good pressure.

name: Alternate wetting and drying (paddy)
description: Field is re-flooded only after standing water disappears to a set level.
notes: Saves water in paddy without yield loss when managed well; keep water at flowering.

name: Mulching
description: Covering soil with crop residue or plastic film.

name: Farm pond
description: Pond to harvest runoff rainwater.
notes: Provides life-saving irrigation in dry spells.

name: Paddy
description: Critical stages are tillering to panicle initiation and flowering. Alternate wetting and drying after establishment saves water; avoid stress at flowering and drain the field about 10–15 days before harvest.

name: Tomato
description: Critical stages are flowering and fruit development. Irregular watering causes fruit cracking and blossom-end rot; drip with mulch works well.

name: Chilli
description: Critical stages are flowering and fruit set. Chilli suffers from both water stress and waterlogging, so ensure good drainage.

name: Banana
description: Banana needs water throughout growth, most critically at flowering and bunch development. Drip irrigation is widely used; avoid prolonged waterlogging.

name: Coconut
description: Coconut needs regular irrigation in summer; water stress reduces nut set in later harvests. Basin or drip irrigation with husk or frond mulch conserves moisture.

name: Sugarcane
description: The formative (tillering) phase and grand growth phase are critical. Irrigation is usually reduced near harvest; confirm timing locally.

name: Groundnut
description: Critical stages are flowering, pegging and pod development; avoid excess water at pod maturity.

name: Cotton
description: Critical stages are flowering and boll formation; avoid waterlogging.

name: Maize
description: Tasselling and silking are the most critical stages; stress then sharply reduces grain set. Maize is sensitive to waterlogging.

name: Brinjal
description: Flowering and fruiting are critical; give regular light irrigation.

name: Onion (small onion)
description: Shallow roots need frequent light irrigation; stopping irrigation about 10 days before harvest improves storage life.

name: Drumstick (moringa)
description: Drumstick is drought tolerant; irrigate at flowering and pod set and avoid waterlogging.

name: Turmeric
description: Needs frequent irrigation in early growth; avoid waterlogging, which favours rhizome rot.

name: Black gram
description: Critical stages are flowering and pod filling; rice-fallow crops grow on residual moisture.

name: Green gram
description: Critical stages are flowering and pod filling; rice-fallow crops grow on residual moisture.
